rows.07:2590c: The boys' restroom or the girls' restroom... which one should I check?
rows.07:25978:
The girls' restroom had four stalls.
It felt a little wrong somehow, but this was no time to worry about that.{p}Where should I search?
rows.07:259f0: The stall at the far end
rows.07:259f8: Second stall from the far end
rows.07:25a08: Third stall from the far end
rows.07:25a3c:
This one, then.
I searched every inch of the stall.
...Nothing.
No good.
I'll search somewhere else.{p}
rows.07:25abc: The boys' restroom had four urinals and two stalls with toilets.{p}Where should I search?
rows.07:25b28: The toilet in the far stall
rows.07:25b3c: The toilet in the near stall
rows.07:25b5c:
I looked over the row of four urinals.
...Nothing seemed out of the ordinary.{p}Where should I search?
rows.07:25bcc:
I decided to check the toilet in the stall.
...Surely it couldn't be inside this toilet bowl, could it?
I searched every inch.
...Nothing.{p}
rows.07:25c6c:
I decided to check the toilet in the stall.
I opened the door.{p}
rows.07:25cc0:
Suddenly, someone came at me!
I threw my arms up to shield my head.
Something toppled against me with a clack.
What the...?
...A deck brush.{p}
rows.07:25d4c:
Had someone propped it up in there as a prank?
Anyway, there didn't seem to be anything here.{p}
rows.07:25dcc:
I decided to check the toilet in the stall.
...Surely it couldn't be inside this toilet bowl, could it?
I searched every inch.
...Nothing.{p}
rows.07:25e70:
I decided to try walking out through the school gate.
What Hino had said might just be a bluff, after all.
Slowly, I tried to step out past the gate.
.........I couldn't.
No matter how often my reason told me it was fine, I was too scared to move my feet.
What if they really did destroy the ampoule?
I didn't know what kind of poison it was.
I couldn't even explain it to a doctor.
I gave up.{p}
rows.07:26000:
I came to the flower bed.
Flowers were always blooming in profusion here.
So I'd always thought of it as a pretty place.
But seen like this, through the darkness of night, it felt somehow eerie.
It was as if something invisible were gathering here.{p}Now, what should I do?
rows.07:26144:
I peered into the flower bed.
In one spot, the soil was heaped up unnaturally.
Could it really be in a place like this?
I began digging up the soil with my bare hands.
The damp, soft earth gave way without any resistance at all.
And what turned up there was...
A stick about the size of a sweet potato.
It was caked in mud, but when I looked closely, one end was rounded.
It bore a small pattern, like eyes and a nose.
In that case, was this a doll?
Judging by its shape, it looked like a kokeshi.
Now that I thought of it, I'd heard something once.
They say the word "kokeshi" comes from "ko-keshi" - "erasing children."
Supposedly, they were first made to mourn babies who couldn't be raised because their families were too poor.
Maybe because it was so crudely made, this kokeshi brought that story to mind.
Perhaps someone had made it by hand.
But why was it in a place like this?
I had no idea.
...There didn't seem to be anything else here.{p}
rows.07:26534:
I came back to the flower bed once more.
I had a feeling there was nothing left worth looking at here.{p}
rows.07:265bc: I decided to go to the home ec room.{p}
rows.07:26694: I decided to go to the home ec room.{p}
rows.07:266c8:
When I tried to open the door, I realized it was locked.
That's right, I have to find the keys.{p}
rows.07:26730: But where am I supposed to go?
rows.07:26750: I decided to go to the home ec room.{p}
rows.07:26778: I'll use the keys I brought from the staff room.{p}
rows.07:267b8: I wasn't very familiar with this room, so I hesitated a little over where to search.{p}Where should I search?
rows.07:26844: I decided to search the shelves.{p}
rows.07:26864:
Bowls, cups and the like were neatly arranged.
The home ec teacher must be a really meticulous person.
There didn't seem to be any space here to hide an ampoule.{p}I'll search somewhere else.
rows.07:2690c: I decided to search the desks.{p}
rows.07:2692c:
Not that there was much to it; there were just eight or so big desks in rows.
I was done searching them in no time.
Looks like that was a waste of time.{p}Now, what should I do?
rows.07:269b4: I decided to go to the home ec room.{p}
rows.07:269e8: I wasn't very familiar with this room, so I hesitated a little over where to search.{p}Where should I search?
rows.07:26a40:
I went to the newspaper club room.
I didn't want to go, thinking of the body lying in there, but I had no choice.{p}
rows.07:26ad0:
...The body was still lying there.
Not a pleasant sight.
I'd better get this over with quickly.{p}Now, what should I do?
rows.07:26b40: I'll try the newspaper club room one more time.{p}
rows.07:26ba8:
I searched the shelves.
There was nothing in particular...{p}
rows.07:26be8:
"Uwaagh!"
Suddenly, a searing pain shot through my leg.
I looked down, and Iwashita was biting into my leg.
...What, had she been hiding under the table?{p}
rows.07:26c90:
"I'll kill you!"
Iwashita lunged at me, her hair flying wildly.
She was clutching a rope in her hands.
Was that the rope that had bound my hands and feet?
I had no time to get my footing back.
As I fell, the rope looped around my neck.
"Die!"
Then Iwashita pulled with all her strength.
"Gaaack!"
In one jerk, the rope cinched tight around my throat.
I tried to tear Iwashita's arms away.
But they wouldn't budge.
I couldn't believe a girl could be that strong.
Little by little, my strength drained away.
I could feel the blood vessels in my head pounding violently, throb, throb.
In a place like this... am I going to die?
I...
The rope strangled me without mercy.
Everything before my eyes was turning red.
I collapsed to the floor.
...Faintly, through the red darkness, I could see Iwashita's triumphant smile.{p}
rows.07:26f38:
I searched the shelves.
There didn't seem to be anything in particular.{p}What should I do?
rows.07:26fac:
...There's a notebook.
On it were written the words "Grudge Notebook."{p}Should I read it?
rows.07:27038:
Better not.
I don't have time for that right now.
I put the notebook back on the shelf.{p}What should I do?
rows.07:270ac:
I opened the notebook.
Inside were petty gripes written by Hino, Shindo and the others.
Spilled coffee on me.
Got barked at by a dog.
Hid my shoes.
Told a stupid joke.
Slapped me on the shoulder out of nowhere.
Was noisy when I was sleepy.
Has a vulgar laugh.
Never apologized.
Paid back the money I lent without interest.
Wouldn't let me copy their notes.
...Along with that petty nonsense, many people's names were written down.{p}
rows.07:27234:
An execution list...
I caught my breath and read on.{p}
rows.07:272c0:
Yo, {a}.
I figured you'd come back to the newspaper club, so I'm leaving this notebook in the shelf for you.
If you find it, read it carefully.
These are the sinners we've killed so far.
There are plenty of reasons why you're getting killed.
You've committed crimes that would justify the death penalty.
The charges are as follows.{p}
rows.07:273b4:
You splashed water on Kazama's pants.
Shindo called out to stop you, and you ignored him.
Arai was standing on the train, and you didn't give him your seat.
You looked at Iwashita and laughed.
You bought the last of the cafeteria curry, so Hosoda couldn't have any.
Fukuzawa stepped on gum you spat out.
And my dad works at the same company as your dad.
Your dad got promoted there, so my dad didn't.
That's why you deserve to die.
Hino.{p}
rows.07:27560:
...I turned to the last page.
At the very end of the notebook, it said this:
A band of people chosen to make this world a paradise.
The Murder Club... it said.
The Murder Club?
I've never heard of a club like that.
Are all of these guys members of the Murder Club?{p}
